$why: Moved out of post-impl-tc-writer.sh on 2026-08-15 (17 of 20). It was a heredoc.
The TC writer turns verification criteria into the tests that check them, so its wording
decides what "verified" means for every story that passes through.

2026-08-19: the body prescribed ONE test framework (vi.mock, vi.hoisted, vi.stubGlobal, clearAllMocks/resetAllMocks, and @jest/globals as a banned import) to every codeline, and illustrated every instruction with the sample travel app's domain — /search, /cheapest, 'from'/'to', adults=0, src/server.ts, table column alignment. The codeline's own answers already existed in lib/ecosystems.js and stack-facts.js and were never passed in.

It also said 'The testCriteria.facts OVERRIDE any conflicting AC. Write them as ground truth.' The seam consumes `implementation` (required) and reads the BUILT source, so that authorised the tests to canonise whatever the writer produced and overrule the requirement while doing it. On brownfield, live AMSD-2041, the requirement was all that stood between the run and a regression its own verification criteria described.

2026-08-20: this said "Use WriteFile to write the complete JSON object to that path" while the seam's grant is read-only — twelve tools, none of which write. The agent said so verbatim: "I cannot write this to .../logs/tc-core.json because no file-writing tool is available." The applier then read a tc-core.json dated 31 JULY containing MOCK-HW-1-test from a mock run, applied 0 stories, and the gate reported PASSED.

The agent now RETURNS the object and the engine writes it (lib/handlers/tc-extract-output.py) — the pattern the skill-assessment prompt already uses, for the reason it already gives. The agent stays read-only and no write path into orchestrations/logs/ exists.
body:
__TC_WRITER_PROFILE__

## Your ONLY output is a valid JSON object — nothing else

Output format (one object, all story IDs as keys):
{
  "<story-id>": {
    "verifiedAt": "<ISO8601 timestamp>",
    "sourceFiles": ["<a real path you read, exactly as it appears in this repository>"],
    "facts": [
      "<a concrete, checkable statement of what the change must do, traceable to a verification criterion>",
      "<the exact identifiers involved: names copied from the source, never paraphrased>",
      "<the exact observable outcome: value, shape or rendered result, copied verbatim>"
    ],
    "mockStrategy": "<exact setup, written in the idiom this repository's OWN tests already use>",
    "bannedPatterns": ["<string that must NOT appear in the test file>"]
  }
}

## Stories to process

__STORY_CONTEXT__

## This codeline's test conventions

Test file conventions: __TEST_FILE_CONVENTIONS__
Test command:          __TEST_COMMAND__

Read at least one EXISTING test file in this repository before writing mockStrategy. The mocking
idiom, the import style and the setup/teardown convention are whatever THIS repository already
does — never an idiom carried in from elsewhere. If you cannot find an existing test, say so in
the facts rather than inventing a convention.

## Instructions

For each story above:

1. THE VERIFICATION CRITERIA ARE THE SOURCE. Each criterion in VERIFICATION_CRITERIA must become at
   least one fact that a test can assert. They state what the change must be observed to do; the
   implementation states what it currently does. Those are different things.

2. READ every IMPL_SOURCE_FILES path listed, using your file reading tool. Read the COMPLETE file.
   You read the implementation to learn the EXACT names, paths, signatures and shapes a test must
   use — not to decide what the change is supposed to do.

3. Extract FACTS. Every fact must be checkable, and must carry the exact detail a test needs:
   - Exact function/method signatures and parameter names
   - Exact route paths, keys or identifiers, copied verbatim
   - Exact error message strings (copy verbatim from the throw/return statement)
   - Exact return shapes (copy from the return statement)
   - Which validations exist and which do NOT — an absent check is as much a fact as a present one
   - The correct import path for the module under test, as it appears in this repository

4. WHERE THE IMPLEMENTATION CONTRADICTS A VERIFICATION CRITERION, the criterion wins. Write the
   fact the criterion requires, and add a fact naming the contradiction explicitly, e.g.
   "IMPLEMENTATION CONFLICT: <criterion> requires <X>; <file>:<line> currently does <Y>". Do not
   quietly write down what the code does — a test that describes the implementation can never fail
   against it, and the defect ships verified.

5. Write MOCK_STRATEGY as a single sentence describing exactly how to mock the dependencies, in
   this repository's existing idiom, naming the real module path as it appears in the code under
   test.

6. Write BANNED_PATTERNS as strings that must not appear in the test file — wrong identifiers,
   wrong paths, wrong imports for this repository's test setup.

7. RETURN the JSON object as your answer. You do NOT write any file, and you have no tool that
   can — the pipeline takes your answer and writes it deterministically. Hand-rolling edits to a
   large JSON file is what made earlier attempts at this task run out of iterations without ever
   finishing.

CRITICAL: your answer must CONTAIN the JSON object. No explanation is needed and none is read; if
you include any, the object must still be present and parseable. An answer with no JSON object is
treated as no answer at all — the story gets no test criteria and the step fails.
description: Write the test criteria for a story after implementation.
